verses.text: Dead flies make a perfumer's oil stink. In the same way, a little foolishness can outweigh wisdom and honor.
A wise person's heart leads them to the right, but a fool's heart leads them to the left.
Even walking down the road, a fool shows how little sense they have. They let everyone know they're a fool.
If a ruler gets angry with you, stay where you are. Gentleness can put even serious offenses to rest.
I've seen another evil under the sun, the kind of mistake that comes from a ruler.
Fools are given positions of honor, while the rich are made to sit low.
I've seen servants riding horses while princes walk on foot like servants.
Dig a pit and you might fall in. Break through a wall and a snake might bite you.
Cutting stone can get you hurt. Splitting wood puts you in danger too.
If your ax is dull and you leave it that way, you'll have to swing harder. Skill is what gets the job done.
If the snake bites before it's charmed, the charmer's words do no good.
A wise person's words are gracious, but a fool gets swallowed up by their own lips.
A fool starts out talking nonsense and ends up spouting destructive madness.
A fool piles on the words. Nobody knows what's coming. Who can tell anyone what will happen after they're gone?
Fools wear themselves out with work. They can't even find their way to town.
Trouble for you, land, when your king is a child and your princes start feasting in the morning!
Good for you, land, when your king is the son of nobles and your princes eat at the proper time to build their strength and keep from getting drunk.
Through laziness the roof sags. When hands sit idle, the house starts to leak.
A feast brings laughter, wine cheers up life, and money is the answer for everything.
Don't curse the king even in your thoughts, and don't curse the rich in your bedroom. A bird in the sky might carry your voice, and something with wings might spread the word.
